clause: A mention sets a working status through assistant.threads.setStatus — which needs `chat:write` and NO new scope (§3.5 S3), so it is the one gain an already-installed app gets with no reinstall
now_false: NOT THE SCOPE CLAIM, WHICH WAS MEASURED AGAINST A REAL WORKSPACE AND HELD — assistant.threads.setStatus really does work on `chat:write` alone, and that answer is kept rather than erased. What is false is that this deployment DOES it. `dfceb769 fix(slack-bot): restore thread text into the run's input, delete 10 dead HTTP-transport exports` deleted slack.SetStatus, agent.go and agent_test.go on the measured ground that nothing in production called them: the 2026-08-05 cutover replaced the in-process HTTP bridge with apps/slack-bot over Socket Mode, and the working indicator became the chat.startStream container headline (relay.go's setHeadline / PlanUpdateChunk). So a mention sets no status, no call is made to that method by anything in this tree, and the sentence's operative half — that an already-installed app GETS this gain — buys nothing. The rest of SLK-009 is unaffected and is re-pointed rather than withdrawn: S12 (blocks on chat.stopStream only) moved to the chunk-mode pair that replaced blocks mode, and S11 (`stopped_by_user` stops the stream and the run keeps running) moved to apps/slack-bot/internal/relay/stopped_test.go, where it is proven more strongly than it was here.
evidence: The live leg that confirmed S3 was deleted in the same commit and its inventory rows are removed with this record (uat.WiringLiveLegs in tests/uat/evidence.go and agentSurfaceLiveLegs in tests/uat/agent-surface/live_inventory_test.go) — both were caught by the inventory's own guard, which says an inventory naming tests nobody wrote is the promise rather than the proof. Measured 2026-08-05: `grep -rn 'SetStatus' --include='*.go' .` finds no production caller of assistant.threads.setStatus anywhere in the tree; the surviving hits are this evidence text, an unrelated coordinator/task-registry `SetStatus bool` field, and two live tests that measure Slack's own behaviour rather than call ours. The same cutover's withdrawal was already recorded for the neighbouring case in tests/uat/tools-memory/catalog_test.go and TLM-003/case.yaml, and S3's confirmed answer is preserved at tests/live/slack/stream_live_test.go's package note: it was CONFIRMED true against a real workspace before the capability it confirmed was superseded.
